text.p: Following are the main stories in Tuesday's Malaysian newspapers. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

-- All newspapers lead with the National Housing Company, which was set up last year, being allocated one billion ringgit to develop low cost housing. The funds are being given by the national oil company, Petronas.

-- Malaysia is to draw up guidelines for fixed line telephone services, the director-general of telecommunications department Hod Parman said. This is to help the many companies entering the fixed line business under Malaysia's liberalisationa and privatisation programme.
-- The police have seized 291 kg of ganja from a cave in the Payar island marine park in one of the biggest haul of drugs in the country so far.
-- RHB Capital Bhd chairman Rashid Hussain denied rumours that his group was planning to take over Bank Bumiputra Malaysia Bhd, the country's second biggest bank.
-- The merged DCB-Kwong Yik Bank, which will be the country's third biggest will be launched on July 7.
